title: IconCanvas
description: Many icons on one canvas, drawn by WebGPU, WebGL2 or WebGL in a few instanced draws, or by Canvas2D: dense pictures, maps, particles and animations of thousands of icons.

intro.title: How it draws
intro.text: IconCanvas places icons by position, size, rotation, color and opacity in CSS pixels, and draws them all on one canvas with the best backend available (WebGPU -> WebGL2 -> WebGL -> Canvas2D).
intro.tessellate: Geometry: each icon is flattened within a quarter of a device pixel and its stroke turned into triangles (a quad per segment, round fans for joins and caps), once per icon, stroke width and level of detail.
intro.batch: Batching: all meshes live in one vertex buffer and every icon is an instance (position, size, rotation, color); consecutive identical icons are one instanced draw call.
intro.depth: Quality: 4× MSAA smooths the edges, and a per-icon depth test draws each pixel of an icon once, so translucent icons blend exactly like the SVG stroke.
intro.fallback: Robustness: auto skips software GPUs, a lost GPU context restarts the backend (a backend lost twice is skipped), and the canvas root reports the backend in data-renderer.
intro.when: For icons in the interface, use Icon: SVG is lighter, accessible and server-rendered. Use IconCanvas when the icons are the picture.

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend preference; `auto` follows the global default

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name of the whole picture (`role="img"`); without it the canvas is hidden from assistive technologies

props.name: items
props.description: Icons to draw, in painting order (later ones on top), positions in CSS pixels

<script setup lang="ts">
// One canvas, one GPU draw per run of identical icons; positions in CSS px.
// The backend follows the global default (setDefaultIconRenderer).
import { ref } from "vue";
import { VStack } from "minerva-design/vue";
import {
  IconCanvas,
  bellIcon,
  homeIcon,
  mailIcon,
  searchIcon,
  settingsIcon,
  userIcon,
  type IconCanvasItem,
  type IconRendererKind,
} from "minerva-design/vue/icons";

const ICONS = [
  homeIcon,
  searchIcon,
  mailIcon,
  bellIcon,
  userIcon,
  settingsIcon,
];
const items: IconCanvasItem[] = [
  ...ICONS.map((icon, i) => ({ icon, x: 16 + i * 48, y: 16 })),
  ...ICONS.map((icon, i) => ({
    icon,
    x: 16 + i * 48,
    y: 64,
    size: 32,
    color: "var(--primary-color)",
    rotation: i * 15,
  })),
  ...ICONS.map((icon, i) => ({
    icon,
    x: 16 + i * 48,
    y: 112,
    strokeWidth: 1.5,
    opacity: 0.35 + i * 0.13,
  })),
];
const drawn = ref<IconRendererKind | null>(null);
</script>

<template>
  <VStack :gap="2">
    <IconCanvas
      :items="items"
      :height="160"
      title="Six icons, three ways"
      @renderer-change="(kind: IconRendererKind) => (drawn = kind)"
    />
    <small role="status">{{ drawn ? `Drawn with ${drawn}` : "…" }}</small>
  </VStack>
</template>

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Icons placed in CSS pixels with their own size, color (theme variables included), rotation, stroke width and opacity.

thousands.title: Thousands of icons
thousands.description: Up to 20,000 animated icons rebuilt every frame and drawn in a few dozen instanced draws (one per kind of icon). The backend follows the renderer bar; compare the frame rate between backends.

renderers.title: Every backend
renderers.description: The same icons forced on each backend; under each canvas, the backend that drew it (a backend this browser lacks falls back to the next one).

IconCanvasProps.items: Icons to draw, in painting order (later ones on top), positions in CSS pixels
IconCanvasProps.renderer: Backend preference; "auto" follows the global default
IconCanvasProps.width: Width; a number is in pixels
IconCanvasProps.height: Height; a number is in pixels
IconCanvasProps.title: Accessible name of the whole picture (role="img"); without it the canvas is hidden from assistive technologies
IconCanvasProps.onRendererChange: Called with the backend once it started, and again after a fallback

IconCanvasItem.x: Left edge in CSS pixels, from the canvas' top-left corner
IconCanvasItem.y: Top edge in CSS pixels, from the canvas' top-left corner

IconStyle.size: Width and height in CSS pixels
IconStyle.color: Any CSS color; currentColor reads the color of the host element
IconStyle.strokeWidth: Stroke width on the 24×24 grid (scales with the size)
IconStyle.rotation: Clockwise rotation in degrees, around the center

IconCanvasHandle.getRenderer: The backend drawing (null until it started)
IconCanvasHandle.ready: Resolves once the backend started and the current items are drawn

props.label: Accessible name of the whole picture (role="img"); without it, the canvas is hidden from assistive technologies
props.canvas: The <canvas> element drawing the icons, null until connected

events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend started, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until it started
methods.ready: Resolves with the backend once it started and the current items are drawn

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: items is a JavaScript property: icons placed in CSS pixels with their own size, color, rotation, stroke width and opacity, drawn on one canvas. minerva-renderer-change reports the backend.
